stage_a.note: The founder is smiling, energetic and consistently positive throughout his pitch.
He shows strong excitement about the product's ability to turn mealtime 'nos' into 'yeses'.
Friendly, approachable and polite demeanor while addressing the panel.

venture.description: Edible organic food paint and condiments in tubes designed to encourage picky children to eat their meals.
venture.note: The product is organic food paint for kids.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo introduces Noshi, an edible organic food paint that helps parents get picky kids to eat their food.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark picks up a box of the product from his sample tray.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori looks through the different boxes of product on her tray.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks to confirm if the founder has a licensing deal with Crayola since it is branded.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo confirms he has licensing deals with Peppa Pig, Crayola, Very Hungry Caterpillar, and Daniel Tiger.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin notes that this means the founder must like royalty deals.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo jokes that he is not averse to royalty deals.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara remarks that the tube seems to contain a very small amount of ketchup for a child.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo explains that a box has three tubes, and one tube is typically split between two kids per mealtime.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks for the retail selling price of the container.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo states that the container sells for $5.46.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks what the product costs to manufacture.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo explains it costs $2.72 to make, but the investment would fund machinery to reduce the cost by 60 cents.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks for the wholesale price of a box of three.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo answers that the wholesale price is $3.70.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark points out that the margins are terrible based on those numbers.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks what the sales figures were for the previous year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo says the sales for last year were $117,000.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks what he projects the sales will be for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo estimates they will end the year at around $200,000, having sold nearly $80,000 so far.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks why the sales are so small and how many stores the product is in.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo states that they are currently in 370 Walmart stores.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks how much of their sales are happening online.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo explains they have zero online sales because of a severe health situation with his wife having long COVID.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks to clarify if his wife is a COVID long hauler.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo confirms she is, noting she had a successful career but won't work again, putting pressure on him.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks where Tomo is based.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo answers he is in New York, and explains his wife moved back to England for care.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark expresses sympathy for the terrible family situation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo elaborates on his priority to keep his kids healthy and happy amidst the circumstances.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks what his career was before this situation occurred.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo shares his background working at Vogue, becoming a stay-at-home dad, and launching the product in 2017 into supermarkets.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara clarifies if the $20,000 in sales came from all of those early stores combined.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo confirms that the sales figure was for all those stores.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks if the low sales were because people did not understand what the product was.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo agrees, explaining that he designed the packaging poorly and it failed to communicate the product.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks to hear the sales numbers for 2018 to understand the trajectory.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo states that sales stayed the same through 2020 because the packaging was still wrong.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks if they managed to stay in those early retail stores.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo confirms they came out of Safeway and Albertsons in 2018.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo tells the story of meeting a Walmart representative at Expo West and securing their licensing deals.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks how Walmart currently feels about their sales performance.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo says they just heard Walmart will put their Sketchup product into 1500 stores next year.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks if they are currently selling through their inventory at Walmart.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo confirms that their last three production runs have completely sold through.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara acknowledges the positive news about the sell-through.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin praises Tomo's resilience but exits due to the lack of sales and the one-man nature of the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo politely accepts Kevin's decision to exit.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara exits because she believes the product belongs in a gift aisle, not the food aisle, doubting its positioning.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo accepts Barbara's decision.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori exits, stating that while it is a clever idea, there is not enough there for her to make an offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo thanks Lori and accepts her decision.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond exits, citing concerns about price resistance from parents paying six dollars for a novelty meal item.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo thanks Daymond and accepts his decision.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks how the product will grab attention quickly on a crowded shelf, noting the difficulty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo argues that the new Crayola packaging will grab much more attention than the previous generic design.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark agrees that the Crayola branding helps.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks what Tomo plans to do to get online sales, as they will be very important.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo says he needs investment funds to produce enough product to sell online.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark hesitates and sighs, trailing off before making a clear statement.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo asks Mark to help him out.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks if Tomo would consider selling single tubes as one-offs from a display basket to encourage trial purchases.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo says he is open to doing anything and reaffirms his belief in the product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark makes an offer of $250,000 for a 25 percent equity stake.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tomo immediately accepts Mark's offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark and Tomo celebrate the deal with a hug.

decisions.note: Kevin exits due to the lack of sales and the one-man show nature of the business.
Barbara exits because she feels the product belongs in a gift aisle, not the food aisle.
Lori exits because there is not enough there for her to make an offer.
Daymond exits due to concerns about parents resisting paying six dollars for a novelty item.
Mark offers $250,000 for 25% equity to help fund online expansion and try selling single tubes.

record.notes: The pitch contains a very personal and emotional story about the founder's wife suffering from long COVID.
